blocks.heading: No Sampled Year-Five Figure Found
rows: Software and AI-adjacent roles Scalable Software skills sell as products, freelance projects and agencies. It is also the most crowded door, so proof decides the pay.

About Rs 3 to 3.5 lakh at general IT-services starts (TeamLease Digital, Sept 2025). Rs 7 to 21 lakh on named specialist tracks at one large firm (Infosys, reported Dec 2025). Average total pay Rs 5.37 lakh under one year (PayScale, 414 salaries, July 2026).
Average total pay Rs 7.54 lakh at 1 to 4 years (PayScale, 3,685 salaries). No sampled year-five figure found.
The 90th percentile base pay is about Rs 20 lakh across all experience (PayScale, 4,950 profiles). Freelance and product income has no verified spread.
Sampled salary site
Data, analytics and business-tech roles Scalable Analysis and reporting sell directly as projects and consulting, and one skill serves many businesses.
No sampled entry figure we trust. Sources disagree, so start from the software floor above and read live listings.
Not found with a sample.
Say less, not more.
No reliable data
Architecture (B.Arch, then registration) Scalable with a business layer A salaried junior is a fixed ladder. A registered practice with your own pricing is the business layer.
Rs 3 to 6 lakh, median about Rs 4.5 lakh (Salaryinsight, April 2026, built from Glassdoor and AmbitionBox, no sample size given).
No verified spread of own-practice income. Treat any single crore-level figure as a famous-firm outlier.
Aggregator, no sample size
Core engineering (mechanical, civil, electrical, electronics) Scalable with a business layer Core jobs follow a fixed ladder. Design, repair, solar or contracting services give the business layer.
Rs 25,000 a month (Rs 3.0 lakh a year) is the formal-work median for all engineering degrees at entry (PLFS 2025, 182 people). We found no branch-wise sampled pay.
Rs 42,000 a month (Rs 5.04 lakh a year) at 3 or more years in the same survey.
42.9% earn Rs 50,000 a month or more at 3 or more years, against 11.2% at entry.
Government survey
Actuarial science (exam ladder) Not so scalable A long exam ladder with pay tied to exams cleared. A consulting layer exists later but few reach it.
Four salary sites average Rs 8.4 to 11.3 lakh for trainee actuaries (2024 to 2025, quoted by the Society of Actuaries, Feb 2026). Their ranges run from Rs 1.09 lakh to Rs 50 lakh.
One author estimate puts 4 to 7 exams cleared at Rs 10 to 15 lakh. It is not survey data.
The same author estimate puts fellows at Rs 25 to 50 lakh or more.
Aggregators, wide range
PSU engineer through GATE Not so scalable A published pay scale and a rank-based entry. The top band is known in advance, and outside work has rules.

NTPC engineering executive trainee notices print grade E1 with Rs 40,000 basic inside a Rs 40,000 to 1,40,000 scale, plus allowances. Seen on exam-prep and job sites, so confirm on the official notice.
Moves by grade and seniority on the published scale.
The top of the scale is printed in the notice. It is a ceiling, not a median.
Reported notice, confirm

blocks.heading: Median Band to the Top Band
rows: Software and data
One language and one real area, such as backend, data pipelines or machine learning basics.
A domain you can speak about, such as finance, health or logistics, plus clear writing.
A deployed project that real people use, a public repository with real commits, and a short note on a bug you fixed.
The jump is moving from a general start to a named specialist track, or to client work you price yourself.
Core engineering
Design, simulation or site-quality skill in one branch.
CAD or simulation software, basic programming, and cost estimation.
A drawing set, a model with calculations, or a site report with before and after numbers.
The jump is moving from execution to design, estimation or a small service you run.
Architecture
Design thinking that survives a site, a budget and a client.
Costing, BIM or CAD depth, and client talk.
A portfolio with process notes and one built or measured project.
The jump is a registered practice with repeat clients and referrals.
Research and quant
Depth in maths, physics or statistics.
Python or R, and plain-English writing.
One dataset analysed from start to finish, or a short literature review with a small project.
The jump is selling the analysis as projects, not waiting for the next post.

blocks.heading: How a PCM Graduate Gets Paid More
rows: Software and data
An employer, or a client who needs a tool, a report or a fix.
A deployed project, a referral from a past client, a clear profile with one specialty.
A one-line position: who you help and with what. Then a simple fixed offer, such as a dashboard for a small shop.
Core engineering
An employer, or a small factory, builder or shop that needs design, repair or a cost estimate.
Site photos, a drawing set, a reference from a supervisor, word of mouth.
A written estimate a client can understand, and a follow-up message after every site visit.
Architecture
A family or business that wants a building planned.
Built work, a portfolio with process notes, referrals from clients and contractors.
Ask every happy client for one introduction, and learn to talk about fees before the drawings start.
PSU, ISRO and research posts
A single employer on a fixed scale.
A rank, a degree and an interview.
Employer-only. The sales layer matters mainly for a side route, such as tutoring, writing or analysis work you sell on the side, or for the move after the post.

blocks.heading: AI By Route
rows: Software

High near term for entry-level work. A revised Stanford study using US payroll data (August 2026) found employment of 22 to 25 year olds in AI-exposed jobs about 19% below where it would be otherwise, driven by less hiring rather than layoffs. It is a US result and the authors call it descriptive, not proof of cause. In India, general fresher pay has stayed near Rs 3 to 3.5 lakh while specialist tracks pay more, so the market is splitting.
Now: use AI to write and test code faster, and show how you checked it. Later: system design, debugging live systems and domain knowledge carry the pay.
Data and analytics
High for routine reports and first-pass charts. Lower for deciding what a number means for a business.
Now: speed up cleaning and drafting, and always verify. Later: choose the question and explain the answer to a client.
Core engineering
Low to medium. Drafting and first-pass analysis get faster. Site judgment, safety calls and accountable sign-off stay with people.
Now: use AI for documents, calculations you then check, and simulation set-up. Later: automation and monitoring skills add a new service line.
Architecture
Medium for rendering and routine drawing. Low for site work, licensing and client trust.
Now: faster concept images and research. Later: cost and BIM depth, where judgment still decides.
Research and actuarial
Medium for literature search and routine analysis. The filter is funding and exams, not tools.
Now: faster reading and code help, always checked. Later: the question you choose is the skill.

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Median pay in the top NIRF engineering band (ranks 1 to 10) is Rs 19.5 lakh. In the bottom band (ranks 151 to 200) it is Rs 4.0 lakh, about 4.9 times lower. Inside one employer type the gap is just as wide: general IT-services fresher pay is about Rs 3 to 3.5 lakh, while named specialist tracks at one large IT firm were reported at Rs 7 to 21 lakh.
